intro.title: Rate limiting at scale
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple rate limiter to control how many requests a server accepts from a client over a set time window. You'll learn the core concept of a token bucket algorithm, which is a common method for managing traffic flow and preventing system overload. The main constructs involved are counters, timestamps, and conditional logic to check request limits. This hands-on exercise will help you understand how large-scale applications maintain stability and fairness under heavy user traffic.
intro.usecase: Rate limiting is essential for protecting APIs and services from abuse or overload in production systems. You'll implement it when building public APIs like those from Twitter or Stripe, where you need to control request volumes per user or IP. This pattern appears in cloud dashboards showing usage quotas, e-commerce checkout flows preventing bot purchases, and streaming services managing concurrent connections. As a developer, you'll configure rate limits to ensure fair usage, prevent DDoS attacks, and maintain system stability under high traffic.
